question: Can a successor cumulative charge record bind one fresh charge identifier to one exact task contract, so a read-only receiver verifies that pair but rejects the same charge identifier when presented by a second task?
objects_and_types: Canonical project-original JSON accounts of profile cumulative-trial-v1, task journals of profile task-reservation-v1, positive bounded integer units, unique bounded text charge identifiers, SHA-256 task-contract coordinates and the directed phase pair charged then reserved.
quantifiers: Nine fixed receiver cases: two exact pairs with distinct identifiers and amounts, one replay of the first pair, two second-task reuse controls, one unit mismatch, one phase error, one duplicate account identifier and one duplicate reservation identifier.
candidate_grammar: The account charge carries charge_id, task_contract_sha256, units and phase=charged. The journal contains the exact task contract and one reservation carrying the same charge_id, recomputed contract digest, units and phase=reserved. A read-only receiver may report BindingVerified only for the exact pair. It never authorizes launch, retry or mutation.
evaluation: Both exact new instances and the exact replay return BindingVerified; every second-task, arithmetic, phase and uniqueness control returns InvalidContext or InvalidEvidence. The same seven-unit amount-only baseline double-matches alpha and beta, while the bound account verifies alpha and rejects beta. All inputs stay byte-identical and no target process starts.
exit: Stop on the first pin, schema, process, output, mutation, classification, accounting or resource failure. Do not repair, refund, launch or grant retry.
protected: A verified binding is not a launch authorization or an exactly-once guarantee
A charge identifier is unique only inside the received finite account
The task digest binds canonical task-contract bytes, not human intent
Directed charged-to-reserved phases are not interchangeable
No refund, automatic retry or target process start
No native free, Close, M6 or arithmetic-universality claim
